# Code style

- STY-001: Follow the Microsoft .editorconfig baseline at the repo root; every rule it adopts is a warning (STY-004 makes warnings fail the build).
- STY-007: Follow Microsoft's C# coding conventions and identifier names. Naming: PascalCase for type names, namespaces and all public members; camelCase for parameters and locals; the s_ prefix for private and internal static fields (STY-014 changes this for static readonly and thread-static fields); the Async suffix on methods that return awaitable types, except where the async page says it doesn't apply (an event handler, a web controller method); meaningful, descriptive names; avoid abbreviations and single-letter names except simple loop counters; no two consecutive underscores. Code: use the using syntax that needs no braces, collection expressions, the concise form of new where the variable type matches, parentheses to make clauses in an expression apparent, a dedicated System.Threading.Lock for a lock statement, && and || over & and | in comparisons, Func and Action over custom delegates, a lambda for an event handler you needn't remove, int over unsigned types, string interpolation for short strings, StringBuilder to append in loops, required properties over constructors that force initialization, static members through their class name, meaningful LINQ query-variable names, and prefer raw string literals. Layout: one statement and one declaration per line, a blank line between method and property definitions, comments on their own line starting with a capital letter and ending with a period.
- STY-014: Where the kit departs from STY-007's pages: a static readonly field that isn't private takes PascalCase, not s_ (Microsoft's field naming guidelines give a public static field PascalCase and no prefix; the identifier names page gives an internal static field s_, which CA1707, checking internal APIs here, fails as an underscore); a thread-static field takes s_, not t_ (a naming rule can't tell a field by its [ThreadStatic] attribute); a constructor that only assigns its parameters is a primary constructor (IDE0290); and an Async suffix isn't required on an event handler, a controller action (MVC trims the suffix, so nameof() in CreatedAtAction would name a missing action), middleware's Invoke or a test method (ADR-0076: a naming rule tripped these, so the owner's decision keeps the suffix advisory).
